dimensionNotes.accuracy: Every narrated number checks out against the research (67 ms, 4 frames, 25 of 27, 258 fetches, checkpoint -1). Two product crops are wrong on screen: one shows the owner's personal project URL under a line about staging, and another crops the root cause mid-sentence so it names the wrong component.
dimensionNotes.depth: The two time-travel bugs are concrete and real, and the 258-request counter is convincing proof. The 'explores' and 'runs on a schedule, against staging' claims rely on narration and kinetic type only, because the explore footage is unused and two schedule crops show the wrong part of the page.
dimensionNotes.clarity: A first-time viewer clearly gets 'records every run and finds timing bugs with a root cause'. Key beats fall short: the film says a time-travel recording can see what video can't but never shows it, 'kept starting over' has no motion, and the silent agent beat is too small to read.
dimensionNotes.story: The arc works: a promise, the product, a fast feature run, a tape-stop turn into 'some bugs only exist in time', two real bugs, then a triad payoff. The differentiator only arrives 43% of the way in, and the end card never prints the closing hook or a clear next step.
dimensionNotes.visual: The hazes, bracketed type and the ch05-s01 rewind turn match the reference well. Broken product crops (a sliced tab bar, a clipped Production card with empty pink placeholders), near-blank intro stamps and a long, mostly empty black player plate in the first bug shot pull it down.
dimensionNotes.sync: Cuts land on bar lines and most type hits land on the spoken word ('67ms' on 'Sixty-seven', the counter stopping dead on 'fifty-eight'). Several beats have nothing to land on: 'background refresh', 'starting over' and 'a time-travel recording can' pass with a static frame.
dimensionNotes.sound: The mix is technically clean (-16 LUFS, a calibrated duck), and the tape-stop, the four-beat hole for 'Four dropped frames' and the played verdict are inspired. The ending has no musical button and is cut 0.8 s after the last word, the payoff line is the most masked in the film, and 'Against staging' is heard as 'Again, staging'.
dimensionNotes.curiosity: The 258 counter and the 25-of-27 ghost renders make you want to see what else time travel catches. The opening sells only convenience, though, and the closing card offers a URL without an invitation, so the pull to try it is softer than the bugs deserve.

summary: Round 1 FAILS the gate (mean 6.82; every dimension below 8; critical issues remain). The narration is accurate and the time-chapter ideas (tape-stop turn, four-beat hole, 258 counter, 25-of-27 grid) are the film's strength. The blocking problem is one root cause: rrweb seeks render a different scroll state in the final render than in the harness, so ch04-s01/02/03 crop the wrong UI; ch04-s02 shows the owner's personal workers.dev URL (critical safety). Fix order: (1) global seek determinism + render-frame crop verification, then ch04-s01/02/03 and ch01-s03; (2) re-take L0402, L0505, L0601 and extend the clock (end-card hold, optional lead-in), then refit ch06-s01/s02 and m01; (3) show the USP and the bug mechanics: ch05-s03 time-travel re-light, ch05-s04 'starting over', ch05-s02 zoom and refresh tag, ch05-s05 legible tagged agent beat, ch03-s01 explore footage; (4) ch06-s02 closing hook on the end card, ch01-s01 early hook seed and contrast, ch02-s01 caret anchoring.
